howto.title: How to Smerge...
howto.intro1: Smerge is a version control system for the block-based language Snap!
howto.intro2: which enables collaboration and tinkering in the classroom.
howto.intro3: It is tailored to novice programmers and therefore easy to use for teachers and students.
howto.intro4: What we wanted to avoid was making a feature-overloaded git clone.
howto.video_intro: The use of Smerge is also explained in this video (English subtitles available) in addition to the following instructions
howto.attention_text: For Smerge to work, JavaScript extensions must be enabled in Snap! To do this, simply click once on the gear in Snap! the first time you open a Smerge project, and check the appropriate box!
howto.badgers_sett_1: A Badger works on his sett, containing a lot of tunnels and chambers, with all his family members and is gradually expanding it over years.
howto.badgers_sett_2: We proceed in exactly the same way while programming: our progress and the further development of the program from version to version we can also present as a 'badger's sett'.
howto.badgers_sett_3: In this example, we are developing asteroids, the game in which you have to destroy all asteroids with your starship before they hit the ship.
howto.badgers_how_1: But how do we come to such a 'badger's burrow'?
howto.badgers_how_2: We can open any of the versions directly in Snap! with a double click. Then we can work on our project, as we are used to.
howto.badgers_save_1: To save the changes in Snap!, we have to 'post' them to our badgers sett.
howto.badgers_save_2: This is done via the corresponding block post to 'smerge...' under Variables. We can summarize what we have done; this way, we will find this particular version of your project later again.
howto.badgers_save_3: Then we can find them in our badgers sett on smerge.org.
howto.collaboration_1: A badger does not work alone on his construction, but with the whole family. Everyone digs their own tunnel.
howto.collaboration_2: It is the same with us when we work collaboratively. We split the work: You work on making the spaceship able to shoot, while a friend or team member handles the asteroids flying through space.
howto.collaboration_3: As you see, everyone is working in his own tunnels! At a certain point the badger wants to meet up with his family members. In the same way, we want to merge our changes to the project.
howto.collaboration_merge: Therefore we simply click the merge button in the bottom right, tick all the versions we would like to merge, and click yes to confirm.
howto.collaboration_result: Now we will find a new version, with all changes merged.
howto.revert: Go back if you made a mistake
howto.revert_text: Sometimes we have to go back to an older version, for example because we made mistakes or tried something that did not work out. Open the version you want to revert to in Snap! and continue from there. This way, you get a new tunnel.
howto.kanban_text: Group work requires communication between participants; for this purpose Smerge provides a Kanban board. It can be opened with a button on the top right below the settings button. Cards can be added, edited, recolored, and dragged between columns.
howto.kanban_columns: To change the column layout, first press the button at the top left and then add, remove, rename or drag columns. You can have up to five columns in total.
howto.for_teachers: Built for teachers and the classroom
howto.for_teachers_text: What does Smerge offer you and how can it help with teaching?
howto.teacher_benefit_1: enabling collaboration for project-based learning with Snap!
howto.teacher_benefit_2: all the data is always available and automatically backed up
howto.teacher_benefit_3: set up templates as code skeletons and add further templates via drag and drop
howto.teacher_benefit_4: the development process is always visible for students and teachers
howto.teacher_benefit_5: version history enables reverting changes and risk-free tinkering
howto.login_text: We deliberately have no dedicated user accounts for average users. To secure projects, you get a PIN at creation time and can set a password.
howto.teacher_view_intro: To access the Teacher View for managing your students' projects, you need to create an account and log in.
howto.teacher_view_1: The teacher view allows you to collect all your students' projects in one place.
howto.teacher_view_2: You can include projects into classes by creating new projects or importing existing ones.
howto.teacher_view_3: You can duplicate projects to share the same starting point with the whole class.
howto.teacher_view_more: Want to know more or need help?

item0.footer:
**__General Movement:
 -Click and drag the mouse on a node to move it
  -Only in "Server-Saved" layout will each move be saved and shared
 -Click and drag outside of a node to move the graph
 -Scroll to zoom in and out

item1.footer:
**__Selecting nodes:
 -Hold Shift or Ctrl and click on nodes to select them
  -Selected nodes have a pink color
 -Hold Shift and drag the mouse to create a selection box

item2.footer:
**__Right click a node to open the context menu:
 - Download: Download corresponding Snap! file.
 - Mark as favorite: Mark a node for all to see.
 - Edit: Change node values.
 - Collapse: Collapse all nodes beneath into one.

item3.footer:
**__Pull a Snap! file into the window dropzone and let go when it is green to upload a file as node.
 - File must have the ending .xml and the Snap! file structure
 - If the file is to big, the download will be refused (if you hit this limit, you might have done somthing pretty wrong)

item0.footer: Double click on a node to open it in Snap!

item1.footer:
**__Activating JavaScript:
 -To be able to use Smerge, JavaScript extensions have to be activated in Snap!
  -Open the Settings menu and check "JavaScript extensions".
 -Click on the "Activate JS and Import Data" block to import your data.

item2.footer:
**__Post to Smerge:
 -Click the "Post to Smerge" block in the tab "Variables" and enter a short description of the new version to upload the changes to Smerge. 
 -If your file size is getting too big (>32MB), the sync will prevent an upload and you need to shrink your file.

item0.footer:
**__Merge two nodes:
 -Select two nodes and click the "New Smerge" button in the right lower corner, then confirm the merge.
 -ATTENTION: If you have a project created before 18.04.24, please use the original merger until you commited all nodes to be merged at least once. Otherwise the new merger won't work correctly!

item1.footer:
**__Solving merge conflicts:
 -If two project versions are too incompatible with each other, they create a merge conflict. Merge conflicts have to be resolved manually. 
  -Double click on a merge conflict to open an overview of conflicting elements. 
  -Select whether to proceed with the left or the right version of the project.

item2.footer:
To change to the old Smerge merger, right click on the "New Merge" button in the lower right corner. The color will change to orange, indicating the change.
Hint: The old merger is capable of merging more than two files at once.

item0.footer:
**__Project setting options:
 -Change Password: updates the password or sets a password if none was set before (requires a password input)
 -Change Project Name: updates the project name (requires a password input)
 -Change Project Description: updates the project description (requires a password input)
 -Delete Project: deletes the project (requires a password input and a confirmation; caution: the deletion is final!)
 -Language: allows to choose the app language

item1.footer:
**__Graph setting options:
 -Save Graph Position: saves the current layout and updates it for all users (if using the Server-Saved layout option).
 -Layout: changes the graph layout. Options include:
  -Dagre: traditional hierarchical layout; default option. 
  -Server-Saved: the custom option saved on the server. 
  -Random: places the nodes randomly.
  -Grid: shows all nodes in the graph on a grid.
  -Circle: organises the nodes into a circle.
  -Concentric: organises the nodes into concentric circles.
  -Breadth First: organises the nodes in levels, according to the levels generated by running a breadth-first search on the graph.
  -Force (Cose): sorts nodes according to an implementation of the CoSE algorithm.
 -Change Scroll Speed: updates the scroll speed used for zooming in or out.
 -Change Project Colors: allows to update the color scheme for normal nodes, nodes marked as favorite and merge conflict nodes.
 -Old Project View: switches to the old Smerge project settings view.

item2.footer: Clicking on "Save Current Layout" downloads the current graph layout as a JSON file to the users' system. The file can be loaded by clicking the "Load Layout From File" button which allows the layout described in the file to be restored.

tutorial.homepage1: Please try again or return to the

welcome.title: Welcome to the interactive Smerge Tutorial!
welcome.description: You will learn how to collaboratively work in Smerge.

overview.title: The project overview
overview.description: You can see how you project has evolved over time.

open_snap.title: Open your project in Snap!
open_snap.description: To work on the project, double-click the blue circle. It will then open your Snap! project.

activate_js.title: Activate JavaScript extensions in Snap!
activate_js.description: Click on on the gear symbol ⚙️ in the top right of Snap! to open the settings menu. Activate 'JavaScript extensions' there.

import_data.title: Import your data
import_data.description: Click on the block 'Activate JS and Import Data' to import your data into Snap!.

edit_snap.title: Edit your project
edit_snap.description: Now you can edit your project in Snap!.  Add new blocks, modify existing ones, or experiment with new ideas. It’s your project, so let your creativity run wild!

post_to_smerge.title: Post your changes to Smerge
post_to_smerge.description: Now its time to save your changes.  Open the “Variables” tab and click the “Post to Smerge...” button at the very bottom. Don't forget to enter a brief description of your changes.

back_to_project.title: Back to the project
back_to_project.description: Your changes are now visible in the project. Click next to see the new version you just created.

view_new_node.title: View your new changes
view_new_node.description: Your changes have been received by smerge. From here, you can continue working on the project at any time.

merge_intro.title: Let's merge!
merge_intro.description: Merging is the process of combining two versions of a project to create a new version. It is an important part of collaboration in Smerge.

merge_select.title: Select versions to merge
merge_select.description:
Another person has been working on the project and created a new version. Let's merge these two versions to create a new version that includes changes from both.
 Hold shift and select the two versions you want to merge. Click on the blue circle to select a version.

merge_click.title: Click the merge button
merge_click.description: Now click the merge button in the bottom right corner to start the merge process. Confirm the merge with the checkbox button.

completion.title: Done!
completion.description: You have successfully merged two versions into a new common version and thus know the basics of Smerge! Have fun with your own projects!

welcome.title: Welcome to the teacher view
welcome.description: Here you can manage classes and student projects.

add_class_button.title: Create a new class
add_class_button.description: Use this plus button in the bottom right corner to add a new class. Give it a name and click create.

add_project.title: Add a project to the class
add_project.description: Click on the plus button to add a new project to the class.

add_project_details.title: Enter project details
add_project_details.description: Enter a name for the project and optionally upload a starting file to provide your students with a template. Confirm with 'Create'.

manage_projects.title: Manage projects
manage_projects.description: The project will now be visible in the class overview. Click on the three dots to open the project context menu. Here you can duplicate the project to create a copy of it, which can be useful to provide all students with the same starting point. You can also delete the project if it is no longer needed.

project_pin_explainer.title: Share projects with students
project_pin_explainer.description: Each project has a unique PIN, which you can share with your students to allow them to access the project. Click on 'Show PIN' to make the PIN visible or copy the PIN directly to the clipboard.

teacher_completion.name: Completed!
teacher_completion.description: You have successfully created a class and added a project to it. You are now ready to use Smerge in your teaching! Have fun teaching and allowing collaborating between your students!
